original.target_description: Analysis 4: ABX error (vowels) correlated with retrieval-induced inhibition across L2 English and L2 Spanish learners; Pearson partial correlation controlling X-Lex proficiency.

n.sample_role: L2 learner participants in the target partial correlation, combined language groups
n.exclusions: Manuscript p. 29 reports 34 of 43 L2 learners with complete data in all tasks (16 L2 English, 18 L2 Spanish). Table 7 explicitly reports n = 33; the additional reduction from 34 to 33 is not explained in the located text. Initial hearing/language-status screening and task-specific exclusions preceded these analyses.

replication.target_description: ABX error (vowels) correlated with retrieval-induced inhibition in L1 English learners of L2 Spanish; Spearman partial correlation controlling X_Lex proficiency.

n.sample_role: Participants: final L2 Spanish sample explicitly named for the Table 10 partial correlations.
n.exclusions: 70 recruited; exclusions: early simultaneous bilinguals/unclear native-speaker status (5), speech/hearing pathology (1), perception control-condition outliers (3), extreme retrieval-induced inhibition value (1), missing production data (2). Table 10 directly prints analytic n = 58. No N arithmetic used.

reported_success.quote: Despite the lack of finding similar effects for the correlation analyses, a comparison of the descriptive statistics indicated comparability between the two studies

notes:
Original locator p. 23 corresponds to published Table 7; the retrieved accepted manuscript has different pagination (Table 7 on p. 32). Replication uses Spearman rather than Pearson because Pearson assumptions were violated (p. 1401). No conversion performed. Original p is a printed one-tailed significance bound from Table 7, not the hierarchical regression p. Reported success records the author’s narrative failure to find similar correlation effects; the quotation concerns the correlation analyses collectively.
Completion source review (n_r): Table 10 directly supplies the analytic sample for these partial correlations. 70 recruited; exclusions: early simultaneous bilinguals/unclear native-speaker status (5), speech/hearing pathology (1), perception control-condition outliers (3), extreme retrieval-induced inhibition value (1), missing production data (2). Table 10 directly prints analytic n = 58. No N arithmetic used.
Completion source review (es_value_r): The explicitly named Table 10 outcome supplies the printed replication partial Spearman coefficient.
Completion source review (pval_value_r): Exact p value belongs to the same replication partial Spearman correlation as the coefficient.
Completion source review (es_value_o): Named outcome matched to the inhibition partial Pearson correlation in Table 7; printed metric retained.
Completion source review (pval_value_o): The star marker on this same Table 7 coefficient is defined by the note as a one-tailed p bound; retain the printed bound rather than substitute a regression p from Table 8.
